'''Diethard Tautz''' (born 17 August 1957 in [[Glonn]]) is a German biologist and geneticist, who is primarily concerned with the molecular basis of the evolution of mammals. Since 2006 he is director at the [[Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Biology]] in [[Plön]].

== Life ==
From 1976 to 1981, Tautz studied biology at the [[Goethe University Frankfurt]] and at the [[University of Tübingen]]. He completed a doctorate in 1983 at the [[European Molecular Biology Laboratory|EMBL]] in Heidelberg and the [[Max Planck Institute]] in Tübingen. He spent two years as a postdoc at the [[University of Cambridge]], UK. From 1985 to 1987, he worked at the [[Max Planck Institute for Developmental Biology]] in Tübingen as a postdoc. After his [[habilitation]] in 1988, he worked as a research group leader at the Max Planck Institute for Developmental Biology until 1990. 

In 1991, he was appointed professor at the Zoological Institute of [[LMU Munich]] in 1991, and at the Institute of Genetics at the [[University of Cologne]] in 1998. Since 2006, Tautz is a "Scientific Member" of the Max Planck Society and director at the Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Biology in [[Plön]].<ref name="Tautz-CV">{{Cite web|url=http://www.leopoldina.org/fileadmin/redaktion/Mitglieder/CV_Tautz_Diethard-D.pdf|title=Diethard Tautz CV|access-date=5 January 2022}}</ref>

== Scientific contribution ==
Tautz's early research included the characterization of simple sequence repeats, now commonly known as [[microsatellite]]s.<ref name="Tautz Renz 1984 pp. 4127–4138">{{cite journal | last1=Tautz | first1=Diethard | last2=Renz | first2=Manfred | title=Simple sequences are ubiquitous repetitive components of eukaryotic genomes | journal=Nucleic Acids Research | publisher=Oxford University Press (OUP) | volume=12 | issue=10 | year=1984 | issn=0305-1048 | doi=10.1093/nar/12.10.4127 | pages=4127–4138| pmid=6328411 | pmc=318821 }}</ref> He later contributed to the development of [[genetic fingerprinting]] methods based on these sequences.<ref name="Tautz pp. 6463–6471">{{cite journal | last=Tautz | first=Diethard | title=Hypervariability of simple sequences as a general source for polymorphic DNA markers | journal=Nucleic Acids Research | publisher=Oxford University Press (OUP) | volume=17 | issue=16 | date=25 August 1989 | issn=1362-4962 | doi=10.1093/nar/17.16.6463 | pages=6463–6471| pmid=2780284 | pmc=318341 }}</ref><ref>Patent Jäckle H & Tautz D (1989) "Process For Analyzing Length Polymorphisms in DNA Regions" europäische Patent Nr. 0 438 512</ref>

During postdoctoral work in [[Tübingen]] with groups led by Herbert Jäckle and [[Christiane Nüsslein-Volhard]], Tautz studied developmental genetics in <nowiki>''</nowiki>[[Drosophila]]<nowiki>''</nowiki>. He cloned and characterized the segmentation gene <nowiki>''</nowiki>hunchback<nowiki>''</nowiki> and contributed to the development of whole-mount [[in situ hybridization]] for studying spatial and temporal patterns of gene expression.<ref name="Tautz Lehmann Schnürch Schuh 1987 pp. 383–389">{{cite journal | last1=Tautz | first1=Diethard | last2=Lehmann | first2=Ruth | last3=Schnürch | first3=Harald | last4=Schuh | first4=Reinhard | last5=Seifert | first5=Eveline | last6=Kienlin | first6=Andrea | last7=Jones | first7=Keith | last8=Jäckle | first8=Herbert | title=Finger protein of novel structure encoded by hunchback, a second member of the gap class of Drosophila segmentation genes | journal=Nature | publisher=Springer Science and Business Media LLC | volume=327 | issue=6121 | year=1987 | issn=0028-0836 | doi=10.1038/327383a0 | pages=383–389| bibcode=1987Natur.327..383T | s2cid=4263443 }}</ref><ref name="Tautz Pfeifle 1989 pp. 81–85">{{cite journal | last1=Tautz | first1=Diethard | last2=Pfeifle | first2=Christine | title=A non-radioactive in situ hybridization method for the localization of specific RNAs in Drosophila embryos reveals translational control of the segmentation gene hunchback | journal=Chromosoma | publisher=Springer Science and Business Media LLC | volume=98 | issue=2 | year=1989 | issn=0009-5915 | doi=10.1007/bf00291041 | pages=81–85| pmid=2476281 | s2cid=37514465 }}</ref>

His  research examined the evolution of developmental processes and segmentation, including work using the beetle <nowiki>''</nowiki>[[Tribolium (beetle)|Tribolium]]<nowiki>''</nowiki> as a model organism.<ref name="Tautz 2004 pp. 301–312">{{cite journal | last=Tautz | first=Diethard | title=Segmentation | journal=Developmental Cell | publisher=Elsevier BV | volume=7 | issue=3 | year=2004 | issn=1534-5807 | doi=10.1016/j.devcel.2004.08.008 | pages=301–312| pmid=15363406 | doi-access=free }}</ref><ref name="Springer Science and Business Media LLC pp. 949–955">{{cite journal | title=The genome of the model beetle and pest Tribolium castaneum | journal=Nature | publisher=Springer Science and Business Media LLC | volume=452 | issue=7190 | date=23 March 2008 | issn=0028-0836 | doi=10.1038/nature06784 | pages=949–955| pmid=18362917 | author1=Tribolium Genome Sequencing Consortium | last2=Richards | first2=S. | last3=Gibbs | first3=R. At LMU Munich, his research expanded to [[population genetics]], speciation, and molecular phylogenetics. His studies included sympatric speciation in cichlids,<ref name="Schliewen Tautz Pääbo 1994 pp. 629–632">{{cite journal | last1=Schliewen | first1=Ulrich K. | last2=Tautz | first2=Diethard | last3=Pääbo | first3=Svante | title=Sympatric speciation suggested by monophyly of crater lake cichlids | journal=Nature | publisher=Springer Science and Business Media LLC | volume=368 | issue=6472 | year=1994 | issn=0028-0836 | doi=10.1038/368629a0 | pages=629–632| pmid=8145848 | bibcode=1994Natur.368..629S | s2cid=4360932 }}</ref> hybrid speciation in European sculpins, and arthropod evolutionary relationships.<ref name="Nolte Freyhof Stemshorn Tautz pp. 2379–2387">{{cite journal | last1=Nolte | first1=Arne W | last2=Freyhof | first2=Jörg | last3=Stemshorn | first3=Kathryn C | last4=Tautz | first4=Diethard | title=An invasive lineage of sculpins, Cottussp. (Pisces, Teleostei) in the Rhine with new habitat adaptations has originated from hybridization between old phylogeographic groups | journal=Proceedings of the Royal Society B: Biological Sciences | publisher=The Royal Society | volume=272 | issue=1579 | date=16 September 2005 | issn=0962-8452 | doi=10.1098/rspb.2005.3231 | pages=2379–2387| pmid=16243698 | pmc=1559961 }}</ref><ref name="Friedrich Tautz 1995 pp. 165–167">{{cite journal | last1=Friedrich | first1=Markus | last2=Tautz | first2=Diethard | title=Ribosomal DNA phylogeny of the major extant arthropod classes and the evolution of myriapods | journal=Nature | publisher=Springer Science and Business Media LLC | volume=376 | issue=6536 | year=1995 | issn=0028-0836 | doi=10.1038/376165a0 | pages=165–167| pmid=7603566 | bibcode=1995Natur.376..165F | s2cid=4270910 }}</ref>

== Memberships ==
From 2005 to 2006, Tautz was president of the German Zoological Society. Since 2009, he is president of the Association of Biology, Biosciences and Biomedicine in Germany (VBIO). He is an elected member of [[European Molecular Biology Organization]] and the [[Deutsche Akademie der Naturforscher Leopoldina]]. He is also editor of scientific journals and, since 2012, senior editor of "eLIFE"<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://elifesciences.org/|title=Latest research|website=eLife|access-date=5 January 2022}}</ref> and since 2014 senior editor of "Molecular Ecology".<ref name="Tautz-CV" /><ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/journal/1365294x|title=Molecular Ecology|website=Wiley Online Library|access-date=5 January 2022|doi=10.1111/(issn)1365-294x|url-access=subscription}}</ref>
